afd.text:
000
FXUS65 KPSR 160811
AFDPSR

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Phoenix AZ
110 AM MST Mon Nov 16 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Warm and dry conditions today will give way to a cold frontal 
passage Tuesday yielding slightly below normal temperatures the 
remainder of the week. 

- A weather disturbance moving through the region Tuesday will 
support chances of showers and locally gusty winds with dry, 
tranquil weather returning Wednesday. 

- Another weather system entering the region Friday will provide the 
next chance of rain focused mainly in higher terrain locations.

&&

.SHORT TERM /Today through Tuesday/...
Early morning WV imagery depicts a shortwave ridge holding over the 
SW Conus while an elongated, sharp trough quickly approaches the 
West Coast. General subsidence should hold over the forecast area 
today, albeit with a gradual increase in cloud cover. Although H5 
heights currently near 580dm will tumble into a 572-576dm range by 
this afternoon, H8 temperatures holding in a +11C to +14C range will 
ensure afternoon highs 2F-5F above normal with efficient mixing 
through the boundary layer. 

Both global and high resolution modeling remain in very good 
agreement showing the trough axis moving onshore early Tuesday 
morning, then rapidly progressing inland through the day. A strong 
meridional component ahead of the trough will cause the system to 
obtain a negative tilt, however also taking the primary vorticity 
center and cold core away from the CWA towards southern Utah. A 
steep cold front with moderate frontogentical forcing will be the 
primary ascent mechanism across Arizona juxtaposed with moisture 
flux in the H8-H7 layer. Given this evolution, the most likely 
outcome will be towards narrow bands of showers developing across 
south-central Arizona along the cold front, potentially with a few 
embedded thunderstorms given modest 100-200 J/kg MLCape in the warm 
sector. Orographic influences north of Phoenix may also aid in 
ascent with the deep southerly flow and moisture advection, though 
the overall trend in high resolution models suggests lower POPs and 
QPF throughout the majority of the CWA.

Elsewhere, gusty winds will be a potential impacts across parts of 
SE California behind the cold frontal passage and coincident with 
strong height falls progressing inland. While not the classic setup, 
sufficient evidence exists showing 30+kt winds in the H9-H8 layer 
mixing off high terrain into lower desert population centers as 
early as Tuesday morning. Some of the more wind prone areas of 
Imperial County may require brief wind advisories during the day 
with blowing dust a concern, although only moderate winds and recent 
rainfall may temper a greater dust threat. Otherwise, the cold front 
should rapidly clear the forecast area by Tuesday evening with 
strong subsidence and a weakening pressure gradient in its wake. 

&&

.LONG TERM /Wednesday through Sunday/...    
Flat ridging/quasi-zonal flow will briefly settle over the SW Conus 
Wednesday before another pronounced trough with strong cyclonic flow 
propagates inland from the East Pacific late in the week. Ensemble 
agreement is excellent maintaining the bulk of the negative height 
anomaly and cold core well into central/northern California and 
Nevada. As such, the jet core should only descend into northern 
Arizona keeping the forecast area under a more anti-cyclonic 
subsident regime. Some moisture may be entrained along a decaying 
cold front Thursday night/Friday, though orographics will likely 
contribute the greatest towards focused ascent. Given this scenario, 
POPs are only highlighted in higher terrain areas with minimal QPF. 
Regardless, this trough passage will reinforce temperatures 3F-6F 
below normal through the weekend with unusually good confidence 
given narrow spread of numerical guidance uncharacteristic for 5 
days in advance during the passage of a weather system. Ensemble 
variations grow substantially late in the weekend due to the 
interaction of Pacific energy with an enhanced subtropical jet. 
While the operational GFS and a handful of GEFS members suggest 
another deepening trough entering the SW Conus, this solution is 
more of a minority versus the entire NAEFS suite with the ensemble 
mean favoring only inconsequential broad cyclonic, or quasi-zonal 
flow towards the end of this forecast period. 

&&

.AVIATION...Updated at 0520Z.

South Central Arizona including KPHX, KIWA, KSDL, and KDVT: 
No aviation weather concerns will exist through the forecast period. 
A light east wind will prevail overnight with speeds mainly aob 6 
kts. Winds are expected to veer out of the SE by Monday afternoon at 
all terminals, but are not expected to fully shift around to the 
west at KPHX. Skies will be mostly clear overnight before FEW-SCT 
high clouds overspread the region early Monday morning and linger 
through much of the day.


Southeast California/Southwest Arizona including KIPL and KBLH: 
No aviation weather concerns will exist through the forecast period. 
Winds will fluctuate between northerly to southerly at KBLH and 
maintain a westerly component at KIPL. Speeds should remain around 7 
kts or less, but will begin to increase out of the west at KIPL by 
Monday evening. SCT-BKN, low cloud decks with bases aoa 8 kft will 
persist with additional high clouds moving into SE California early 
Monday morning.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER... 
Dry conditions with temperatures slightly above normal today will 
give way to increased rainfall chances and cooler temperatures 
Tuesday. Wetting rain chances Tuesday are only 20-50% over upslope 
areas north and east of Phoenix, while locally gusty winds affect 
parts of western districts. Otherwise, minimum afternoon humidity 
levels will fall into a 20-30% range in western districts and 30-50% 
across eastern districts. This will follow good to excellent 
overnight recovery of 60-100%. Another weather system moving through 
the region Friday may provide another round of rain, but mostly 
confined to higher terrain north and east of Phoenix while 
reinforcing cooler temperatures. 

&&

.HYDROLOGY...
Gila: A Flood Warning remains in effect from Painted Rock Dam 
through the Dateland area through at least the next couple days due 
to water released from the dam. Water releases remain around 3000 
cfs. This will have the potential to flood farm fields and low water 
crossings along the river downstream from the dam.

&&

.PSR WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
AZ...None.
CA...None.

&&

$$

SHORT TERM...18
LONG TERM...18
AVIATION...Salerno
FIRE WEATHER...18
HYDROLOGY...Lojero
